title: Bank CSV Intake Check
user: A self-employed person or bookkeeper importing a bank CSV who needs to know, before changing books, whether the file parsed completely and which rows are ambiguous.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A small-business-finance discussion describes repetitive work normalizing data from banks, cards, and invoices before deterministic reconciliation.
An Actual user reports that a downloaded bank CSV import appears to do nothing in both Firefox and Chromium, leaving them to inspect devtools.

recurrence: Two independent finance-tool contexts in 2025–26; import failure or silent row loss prevents reconciliation and is severe because books may look complete when they are not.
current_workaround: Retry an import, edit CSV headers and encodings in a spreadsheet, then manually compare balances and row counts.
incumbents_and_gap: Actual, Firefly III, YNAB, and bank-specific importers ingest files, but the user usually learns parsing assumptions only after importing into a live ledger.
smallest_useful_product: Local drag-and-drop CSV/OFX preflight that identifies delimiter/encoding/date/decimal assumptions, duplicate and missing transaction candidates, balance coverage, and emits a scrubbed import report. Non-goals: bank connectivity, bookkeeping, categorization, or tax advice.
success_measure: In a pilot of 30 files, the report agrees with the target ledger's accepted row count and total within one row/cent in at least 95% of files.
monetization: one-time — this is an episodic, privacy-sensitive handoff check rather than an accounting subscription.
constraints: All parsing in-browser; never transmit transaction data; clearly label heuristics; support locale-specific CSV safely and do not make accounting assertions.
why_distinct: It is a reversible pre-import evidence step, not another personal-finance ledger.

title: Payout Reconciliation Casefile
user: A small ecommerce operator or their accountant who needs to explain exactly why an order, processor payout, and ledger total do not agree.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An ecommerce reconciliation prototype author asks operators and accountants what is most frustrating about connecting Shopify, payment providers, and accounting software and explaining mismatches.
A finance-import issue reports a pagination request that silently drops all transactions for large-history accounts, the exact class of discrepancy that needs an auditable explanation.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 finance contexts; one explicitly seeks mismatch explanations and another documents silent transaction loss, a high-severity close-of-books risk.
current_workaround: Export CSVs from Shopify, Stripe/PayPal, and accounting software; use VLOOKUPs and manually annotate exceptions in a spreadsheet.
incumbents_and_gap: A2X, Synder, Link My Books, and accounting suites automate posting, but small operators need a neutral, source-file-based casefile before trusting an automation or escalating an exception.
smallest_useful_product: Offline matcher for three CSV exports that groups expected fees, refunds, timing windows, and unmatched records into shareable Markdown/CSV casefiles. Non-goals: connecting accounts, posting journal entries, VAT calculation, or automated bookkeeping.
success_measure: For a seeded 1,000-order dataset, it assigns a reason or a bounded exception group to at least 90% of unmatched amount without manual row-by-row filtering.
monetization: one-time — periodic reconciliation benefits from a local tool with no ongoing access to financial accounts.
constraints: Local-only processing; configurable fuzzy-match windows; no tax or accounting advice; reports must redact customer identifiers by default.
why_distinct: It creates explainable exception evidence from exports rather than competing as an ecommerce accounting system.

title: Availability DST Audit
user: A consultant, recruiter, or distributed team coordinator who needs proof that published booking availability respects intended local working hours across daylight-saving changes.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A planner builder says schedules cannot remain fixed because meetings and delays move; the tool's stated core value is adapting plans when reality shifts.
Cal.com documents afternoon slots shifting one hour late on DST transition dates, allowing booking outside the organizer's stated 1–6 PM window.

recurrence: The schedule-adaptation request and a concrete 2026 booking failure independently expose fragile time handling; a wrong slot causes missed meetings and loss of trust.
current_workaround: Manually inspect a booking page around DST weekends, add buffer blocks, or wait for invitees to report wrong times.
incumbents_and_gap: Calendly, Cal.com, Google Calendar, and Cron have scheduling engines, but none is a vendor-neutral preflight that turns declared availability into a human-reviewable DST test matrix.
smallest_useful_product: A static web tool that accepts weekly hours, IANA zones, and a date range, then renders overlap/DST boundary cases and exports an ICS/CSV expected-slot fixture. Non-goals: calendar sync, booking pages, reminders, or AI scheduling.
success_measure: For a known DST boundary fixture, it flags every intentionally shifted slot and produces an expected-slot table in under 30 seconds.
monetization: free — transparent timezone rules and shareable fixtures are more valuable than locking users into a scheduler.
constraints: Use the IANA timezone database; explain local-time ambiguity; do not claim parity with every vendor's proprietary availability logic.
why_distinct: It tests scheduling claims rather than replacing a calendar or booking product.

title: Rename Plan Reviewer
user: A person preparing a batch rename from a spreadsheet or rule who needs to spot collisions, broken numbering, and unsafe paths before files are touched.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A browser-based batch-renamer was built specifically because new filenames already existed in Excel or a spreadsheet rather than following a simple pattern.
A File Manager user requests regex or character-substitution renaming, confirming ongoing demand for rule-driven renames rather than one-file edits.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 requests span spreadsheet mappings and regex rules; mistakes are destructive and especially costly in document/photo archives.
current_workaround: Run a rename command or GUI preview, copy mappings into Excel, back up first, and undo manually after discovering collisions.
incumbents_and_gap: PowerRename, Advanced Renamer, Finder, and bulk-renamer apps perform renames; their previews rarely make a spreadsheet/rule mapping a portable, reviewable change plan with dependency ordering.
smallest_useful_product: Local browser app that imports a current→new CSV or regex rule, validates path portability/collisions/cycles, computes a safe two-phase order, and exports a shell/PowerShell plan plus undo manifest. Non-goals: file browsing, cloud sync, or executing deletion.
success_measure: On a fixture with swaps, duplicates, reserved names, and 1,000 mappings, it identifies 100% of unsafe mappings and outputs a reversible plan without changing files.
monetization: one-time — a careful batch-renaming utility has project-based value and no need to retain files.
constraints: Never upload paths; quote generated scripts for each platform; default to dry-run; explicitly warn about case-insensitive and Unicode-normalization filesystems.
why_distinct: The primary output is a reviewed and reversible rename manifest, not another file manager.

title: File Change Space Check
user: Someone copying, extracting, or reorganizing a large local folder who needs a correct free-space and conflict estimate before starting a long operation.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A request for real-file AI workflows explicitly lists renaming/organizing documents and cleaning spreadsheets as multi-step tasks people try to perform on their actual files.
A File Manager bug report says copy operations calculate required storage before the conflict-resolution dialog, producing an incorrect decision sequence.

recurrence: A broad real-file workflow request plus a concrete Android copy-order defect show that file operations are still unreliable at the plan stage; failure can strand a partially copied archive.
current_workaround: Estimate folder size in a file manager, start copying, then cancel or manually clear space when conflicts and duplication change the required capacity.
incumbents_and_gap: Finder, Explorer, rsync, robocopy, and Android file managers execute operations, but few offer a standalone what-if simulation accounting for overwrite/skip/keep-both policies before an action begins.
smallest_useful_product: Desktop CLI that scans source/destination metadata, lets users select a conflict policy, estimates net bytes and temporary headroom, and emits a deterministic action manifest. Non-goals: file transfer UI, cleanup recommendations, or deleting anything.
success_measure: Against fixtures with duplicates and conflicts, estimated post-policy bytes are within 2% of the actual result and all insufficient-space cases are flagged before execution.
monetization: free — portability and trust improve if the estimator remains a small inspectable utility.
constraints: Metadata scan only by default; account for sparse files and filesystem allocation uncertainty; never assume permissions or execute the manifest.
why_distinct: It plans a file operation under explicit policies instead of becoming a file manager or cleaner.

title: Notes Import Preflight
user: A person moving years of notes between tools who needs to measure what content, attachments, links, and metadata will survive before committing to an import.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A tool author says Apple Notes exports need to preserve folders, formatting, images, and voice recordings, demonstrating the breadth users expect from a real export.
A Joplin user reports a normal 150 MB OneNote notebook failing during import with WebAssembly out-of-memory despite substantial free RAM.

recurrence: Two distinct 2026 migration contexts show both fidelity and scale failure; users risk abandoning an import after losing information they cannot easily reconstruct.
current_workaround: Run an importer against a copy, manually inspect a few notebooks, split archives, and discover missing assets or failed notes afterward.
incumbents_and_gap: Apple Notes export, Joplin, Obsidian importers, and one-off migration apps perform conversion; they do not offer a neutral, local before/after inventory that identifies unsupported constructs before migration.
smallest_useful_product: Local CLI that inventories an export archive, reports counts/types/attachment sizes/link targets, samples conversion-risk features, and compares a destination export for loss. Non-goals: account access, cloud sync, OCR, or a notes editor.
success_measure: For supported export fixtures, it finds 100% of intentionally missing attachments and reports notebook/note counts before a destination import is started.
monetization: one-time — data migration is episodic and users should not pay recurring fees to inspect private archives.
constraints: Run locally; parsers must treat archives as untrusted; do not bypass application encryption or scrape accounts; preserve only aggregate diagnostics by default.
why_distinct: It is a migration quality gate, not another notes app or importer.

title: Identity Migration Map
user: A self-hoster or small-team administrator changing a user identifier who needs to inventory every dependent path, record, and integration before a rename.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A chat-migration tool was motivated by no easy way to move a large private knowledge base without manual copy/paste or trusting a third-party web script.
Nextcloud users request user-id migration support and explicitly note that dependent apps must rename their own tables safely.

recurrence: Two 2026 migration requests in unrelated ecosystems show the same handoff problem: identity changes fan out into opaque dependencies and manual work.
current_workaround: Create a new account, copy selected data, grep configuration/databases, or leave a legacy identity in place indefinitely.
incumbents_and_gap: Individual products offer account exports and sometimes rename commands, but there is no small local planning artifact that makes identifier dependencies, unhandled systems, and rollback boundaries explicit.
smallest_useful_product: A local manifest generator taking declared identifier mappings plus filesystem/config/database read-only exports and producing dependency hits, owner checklists, and a rollback ledger. Non-goals: changing accounts, provisioning identity, SSO, or automated database writes.
success_measure: On a seeded repository/config fixture, it finds every declared old identifier occurrence and produces a complete owner checklist in under five minutes.
monetization: one-time — identity migrations are rare, security-sensitive projects best handled offline.
constraints: Read-only inputs; support secret redaction; never infer authorization from a string match; state clearly that external SaaS dependencies require human confirmation.
why_distinct: It plans and evidences an identity handoff without becoming an IAM product.

title: Knowledge Handoff Bundle
user: A departing project owner or small team handing work to someone else who needs a durable, browseable package showing the current source of truth, linked files, and unresolved gaps.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A team asks how others track organizational knowledge when context is out of date, sources of truth are unclear, and finding an expert is difficult.
A Linkwarden migration bug shows an operator can set a small fractional import cap and have every import rejected while the error reports a misleading limit.

recurrence: A direct knowledge-context question and a concrete import/handoff failure both occurred in 2026; incomplete transfer makes new owners waste time re-discovering decisions.
current_workaround: Send a wiki link collection, shared drive folder, and a free-form handover document; recipients discover expired links and absent context later.
incumbents_and_gap: Notion, Confluence, Linkwarden, and shared drives store content, but they do not create a local, versioned handoff packet that makes reachable links, file hashes, owners, and acknowledged gaps first-class.
smallest_useful_product: A CLI that turns a YAML checklist and local files/URLs into a static handoff site with manifest, link checks, ownership fields, expiry warnings, and a recipient acknowledgement export. Non-goals: wiki hosting, crawling private systems, or AI summarization.
success_measure: In a handoff trial, a recipient can identify every required artifact and every broken/expired link from the bundle without accessing the former owner's notes.
monetization: free — a transparent file format and static output are essential to a trustworthy handoff utility.
constraints: Never fetch authenticated URLs without explicit user-supplied credentials; avoid storing secrets in generated sites; link checking must respect rate limits and robots controls.
why_distinct: It is a portable, verifiable handoff artifact rather than another knowledge base.

title: Passkey Extension Check
user: An employee or privacy-conscious multi-browser user who needs to discover whether installed password-manager extensions can conflict before a passkey is their only login route.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A Chrome password-manager user asks about browser versus standalone managers, citing passkey synchronization, browser isolation, multiple browsers, and the pain of copying databases.
A 30-comment Bitwarden issue reports passkeys completely broken when 1Password is co-installed, including corporate environments where users cannot disable the other extension.

recurrence: The independent architecture question and high-discussion coexistence defect show a real 2026 transition risk; a failed passkey can lock a user out of a critical account.
current_workaround: Disable extensions one at a time, use an alternate browser/device, or discover the conflict only during authentication.
incumbents_and_gap: Browsers, Bitwarden, 1Password, and enterprise management install/manage credentials but do not give users a neutral local compatibility and recovery-readiness report across installed extensions.
smallest_useful_product: A browser extension that inventories password/passkey provider extensions and browser settings, runs a non-secret WebAuthn capability check, and generates a remediation/recovery checklist. Non-goals: storing credentials, intercepting authentication, or bypassing enterprise policy.
success_measure: On test profiles with known conflicting providers, it identifies the conflict and recommends a valid recovery route before the user attempts a real passkey login.
monetization: free — trust requires inspectable, no-account diagnostics; enterprise deployment support could be paid later.
constraints: Never read passwords, passkeys, or page form values; use only documented extension/browser APIs; avoid security guarantees and disclose browser-specific limitations.
why_distinct: It diagnoses passkey-provider coexistence instead of competing as a password manager.

title: Document Integrity Receipt
user: A person handing off a signed or important PDF who needs a simple local receipt of page, hash, signature, and derivative status so recipients know what they received.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A multilingual personal-document-server request describes scanning invoices, medical papers, and government documents and struggling to find and manage them across languages.
A PDF.js bug reports that exporting one edited page leaves digital-signature information in the output document, confusing the integrity status of the derivative.

recurrence: A personal-records workflow and a concrete signature-metadata failure show that important document handoffs need clearer provenance; misleading signature state can create legal or administrative confusion.
current_workaround: Email the PDF with a note, inspect viewer-specific signature panels, or trust filename/version conventions.
incumbents_and_gap: Adobe Acrobat, Preview, PDF.js, and document-management systems can display or edit PDFs, but a lightweight local receipt for the exact handoff artifact is not their primary product.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PDF inspector that generates a sidecar HTML/JSON receipt containing file hash, page count, embedded-signature presence/validation status where supported, detected modifications, and a clear derivative warning. Non-goals: signing, legal validation, OCR, document storage, or editing.
success_measure: For fixtures containing an intact signed PDF and an edited derivative retaining signature metadata, the receipt clearly distinguishes the two with no false claim of valid content integrity.
monetization: one-time — document provenance checks are sensitive and need no hosted storage.
constraints: All files remain local; distinguish cryptographic signature validity from legal validity; use audited PDF libraries; never offer legal advice.
why_distinct: It provides a handoff receipt for an existing document, not a PDF editor or e-signature platform.

title: A11y Interaction Trace
user: A web developer or accessibility tester who needs a small reproducible record of keyboard focus, visible UI, and accessibility-tree changes for a broken interaction.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A developer asks for open-source tools to capture both the screen and accessibility tree while keeping all data private and local.
A reproducible shortcut issue shows that holding the Windows key can make Clipboard History and Voice Typing disappear, illustrating interaction failures that need better evidence than prose.

recurrence: A direct local a11y-tree capture request and a separate keyboard-accessibility interaction defect in 2026 demonstrate recurrent, difficult-to-describe failures.
current_workaround: Record a screen video, paste screenshots into an issue, manually describe focus order, and hope the receiving developer can reproduce it.
incumbents_and_gap: Playwright, axe, Accessibility Insights, and OS screen recorders test or record pieces of the problem; none produces a compact local timeline joining keyboard actions, focus target, screenshots, and selected ARIA snapshots for handoff.
smallest_useful_product: Browser extension that records explicitly started test sessions, captures keyboard/focus events, opt-in screenshots, and a narrowed accessibility snapshot, then exports a self-contained trace viewer. Non-goals: continuous surveillance, automated remediation, general analytics, or uploading sessions.
success_measure: A reviewer can reproduce a seeded focus-trap defect from an exported trace without a live screen share, and the trace records each keyboard action/focus target correctly.
monetization: free — local issue bundles are most useful when teams can share them without a service account.
constraints: Default to local-only; mask typed text and sensitive fields; require visible recording state; scope snapshots to the tested tab and honor browser permission limits.
why_distinct: It is a reproducibility handoff artifact, not another automated accessibility scanner.

title: Remote File Handoff Manifest
user: A freelancer or small team sending a private folder through a NAS, SFTP, or peer-to-peer link who needs a recipient-verifiable inventory instead of an ambiguous 'uploaded' message.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A private WebRTC file-transfer alternative was motivated by an abandoned service and concern about tracking and data collection.
A File Manager request asks for SFTP, Samba, and other remote filesystem support, reflecting the need to work across non-cloud file locations.

recurrence: Two independent file-transfer/storage requests in 2025–26 show demand for privacy and heterogeneous destinations; missing or altered deliverables create costly client handoffs.
current_workaround: Send a link and manually list filenames in an email; recipients compare folder contents visually or request a resend after an incomplete download.
incumbents_and_gap: WeTransfer, Send, Syncthing, SFTP clients, and NAS products move bytes, but their completion screens are not a portable, signed folder manifest that a recipient can verify through any transport.
smallest_useful_product: CLI that builds a signed JSON/HTML manifest with relative paths, sizes, hashes, optional expiry/contact fields, and a recipient-side verifier; optional SFTP/NAS upload only copies the package. Non-goals: hosting storage, authentication brokering, encryption-key custody, or large-file transfer infrastructure.
success_measure: When one file is missing or altered in a 10,000-file fixture, recipient verification identifies the exact path and no unchanged file is reported as bad.
monetization: free — an open manifest format is needed for cross-tool verification; paid support can follow if usage warrants it.
constraints: Hash filenames can reveal private information, so offer encrypted/opaque manifests; use standard cryptographic libraries; never advertise delivery guarantees when transport is external.
why_distinct: It supplies transport-independent evidence of a handoff rather than becoming another file-transfer service.
